en.name: Lawrence of Brindisi
en.summary: Capuchin friar and Doctor of the Church, a gifted linguist who preached across Europe and once led an army into battle carrying only a crucifix.
en.body: Lawrence of Brindisi entered the Capuchin Franciscan order and became renowned for an extraordinary command of languages, reportedly fluent in his native Italian along with Latin, Greek, Hebrew, German, French, and Spanish, which he put to use preaching effectively to diverse audiences and, on at least one occasion, debating Jewish scholars in fluent Hebrew. He held senior leadership roles within the Capuchin order and undertook demanding diplomatic missions on behalf of the papacy and Catholic rulers, at one point accompanying an imperial army against Ottoman forces in Hungary, where, unarmed and carrying only a crucifix, he rode at the front rallying the troops during a decisive battle. He continued undertaking difficult diplomatic journeys well into old age, dying in 1619 during one such mission to Lisbon. He was canonized in 1881 and declared a Doctor of the Church in 1959.
